correctness.rationale: For the angular-frequency normalization, the off-diagonal Hilbert-Schmidt square equals the explicitly positive sine-kernel integral. The Fourier moment F(t)=4sin(at/2)sin(bt/2)/t^2 and a uniform D^-1 denominator expansion give the exact leading J and J' terms with controlled remainders. Differentiating under compact integrals gives the J'' asymptotic; in the nonresonant case J' has exactly one late simple root per half-period by sine sign away from each root and fixed cosine sign close to it. In the mixed-resonance case |2WF'(2W)|<ab follows from |sin z|<z, so J'<0 eventually regardless of phase. The package check.py passed 132 independent symbolic/quadrature tests. These finite tests do not prove the infinite part, which follows analytically.

value.rationale: The exact mixed-resonance criterion concerns a natural invariant: quadratic transition leakage of a two-component Slepian concentration operator. For unequal widths, resonance of only one window is sufficient and necessary to suppress infinitely many large-gap oscillations; the competing O(D^-3) derivative term is shown to be definitively negative. The theorem gives the sharp oscillatory O(D^-2) envelope and all late stationary-point types, directly refining a published symmetric classification and separating a genuinely asymmetric parameter regime. No claim is made for individual eigenvalues or for a universal finite threshold.
